layers.label: Private land
layers.about: Private parcels, merged into blocks. You need the owner's permission to hunt here. Owner names are not open data in BC. Not every parcel is fenced or signed.

layers.label: Crown land
layers.source: WHSE_CADASTRE.PMBC_PARCEL_FABRIC_POLY_SVW (ParcelMap BC owner type), with reserves, treaty lands, parks and municipalities cut out; lakes, wide rivers and reservoirs (WHSE_BASEMAPPING.FWA_LAKES_POLY, FWA_RIVERS_POLY, FWA_MANMADE_WATERBODIES_POLY) cut out
layers.about: Public provincial land. Hunting is usually allowed here in an open season. Light green is derived: land with no titled parcel.

layers.label: Crown tenures (leases, licences)
layers.source: WHSE_TANTALIS.TA_CROWN_TENURES_SVW (Crown land tenures, in good standing)
layers.about: Leases, licences of occupation, permits and rights of way on Crown land. Hunting is often allowed, but check for buildings, fences and signs.

layers.label: Range tenures (grazing, Range Act)
legend: Grazing or hay cutting licence or permit (Range Act)
layers.about: Crown land where someone holds a Range Act grazing or hay cutting licence or permit. Cattle may be out. Respect gates and fences.

layers.label: Where you can likely hunt
legend: Likely open to hunt (check season, MU and signs)
Check first: tenure, federal land or park
layers.source: Derived: Crown land layer minus no_hunting, municipalities, tenures and federal land; parks as check first; lakes, wide rivers and reservoirs (WHSE_BASEMAPPING.FWA_LAKES_POLY, FWA_RIVERS_POLY, FWA_MANMADE_WATERBODIES_POLY) cut out
layers.about: Derived. Never a sure yes: the season, MU (Management Unit), signs, closures and the 100 m rule still decide.

layers.label: Parks and protected areas
layers.about: Provincial parks, ecological reserves and protected areas. Hunting rules differ by park.

layers.label: Reserves
layers.about: First Nations reserves. Hunting needs permission from the Nation.

layers.label: City and town limits
layers.about: Cities, towns and villages. Most ban shooting inside their limits by bylaw. Check the local bylaw.

layers.label: Wildlife Management Areas
layers.about: Crown land set aside for wildlife. Hunting is often allowed, but some have their own rules. Read the area notes.

layers.label: No shooting / no hunting areas
layers.source: Synopsis 2026 to 2028 and Closed Areas Regulation rules, drawn on official outlines: TA_PARK_ECORES_PA_SVW, CLAB_NATIONAL_PARKS, ABMS_MUNICIPALITIES_SP, TA_WILDLIFE_MGMT_AREAS_SVW, FWA_LAKES_POLY, FWA_ISLANDS_POLY, GBA_LOCAL_REG_GREENSPACES_SP, PMBC_PARCEL_FABRIC_POLY_SVW and the MU 3-45 outline
layers.about: Areas where hunting or shooting is banned, drawn only where the legal area is an official outline (BC wide: ecological reserves and national parks; Regions 1 and 2: regional district parks plus 100 m; Region 2: Burns Bog, Bowen, Keats, Savary and North Thormanby islands, seasonal Garibaldi Park and Cultus Lake; Region 3: the closures listed in the Rule Book that follow an official outline). Most No Shooting Areas are not drawn: see the synopsis maps.

layers.label: Management Units
layers.about: Seasons and limits are set by MU (Management Unit). Check the unit before you hunt.

layers.label: Management Unit numbers
layers.about: Unit numbers like 3-27.

layers.label: Limited Entry Hunting zones
layers.about: Zones where some seasons need a Limited Entry Hunting draw permit. Zones overlap by species.

layers.label: Motor vehicle closures
layers.about: Motor Vehicle Closed Areas and ATV (all terrain vehicle) closures from the hunting synopsis maps.

layers.label: Routes in closures
layers.about: Roads open or closed to motor vehicles inside closures.

layers.label: Forest Service roads
layers.about: Resource roads on the forest tenure list. A road on the map can be gated, washed out or deactivated.

layers.label: Recreation sites
layers.about: Free or low cost campsites run by Recreation Sites and Trails BC.

layers.label: Recreation trails
layers.about: Official trails from Recreation Sites and Trails BC.

layers.label: Detailed roads (class, surface, status)
legend: Class unknown in the road atlas
Forest tenure road, not in the road atlas
Grey dashes: retired, overgrown or decommissioned
Blue grey dashes: proposed or pending, may not exist
layers.source: WHSE_BASEMAPPING.DRA_DGTL_ROAD_ATLAS_MPAR_SP (BC Digital Road Atlas: class, surface, lanes) and WHSE_FOREST_TENURE.FTEN_ROAD_SEGMENT_LINES_SVW (forest tenure road segments: life cycle status)
layers.about: Resource, service, recreation, restricted access and unknown type roads from the BC road atlas, plus logging roads on permit records (active, retired or pending). Town streets are on the base map. Most unnamed lines were traced from air photos: the province says not to use them to navigate. Gates are not on this map. A line on the map is not a promise the road is open, drivable or legal to drive. Roads can be gated, washed out, snowed in, deactivated or inside a motor vehicle closure: check the Motor vehicle closures layer, the synopsis and posted signs.

layers.label: Trails and old tracks (road atlas)
layers.source: WHSE_BASEMAPPING.DRA_DGTL_ROAD_ATLAS_MPAR_SP (road atlas trail class). OpenStreetMap tracks and paths were not reachable when built
layers.about: Trails, skid trails and old tracks the road atlas maps, beyond the official recreation trails, plus some paved town walkways. A trail on the map is not a promise it is open, passable or legal to ride: closures, private land and posted signs still apply.
legend: Purple dots: trail or old track

layers.label: Shooting ranges and clubs
layers.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, through the Overpass API: leisure=shooting_ground, sport=shooting or archery, shooting=*
layers.about: Shooting ranges, gun clubs and archery ranges mapped in OpenStreetMap, all of BC. Volunteer mapped: some clubs are missing, some may have closed. Website and phone only where the data has them. Membership or day fees may apply: call first (Tip).
legend: Pistol, more than one type, or type not in the data

layers.label: Mule deer winter range
layers.about: Official ungulate winter range. Deer gather here from about November to April. None is mapped near Heffley Creek.

layers.label: White tailed deer winter range
layers.about: Official white tailed deer winter range.

layers.label: Moose winter range
layers.about: Official moose winter range.

layers.label: Elk winter range
layers.about: Official elk winter range.

layers.label: Bighorn sheep winter range
layers.about: Official bighorn sheep winter range.

layers.label: Mountain goat winter range
layers.about: Ungulate winter range for mountain goats, set by government order.

layers.label: Burns by year
layers.about: Fires since 2000. Burns 3 to 15 years old grow food for deer, moose and bears.

layers.label: Cutblocks by age
layers.about: Logged openings 25 years old or less. Blocks 5 to 20 years old feed deer, moose, bears and grouse.

layers.label: Wetlands
layers.about: Marshes, swamps and bogs from the Freshwater Atlas. Good for moose and ducks.

layers.label: Habitat zones
layers.about: Biogeoclimatic zones: the plant community you will find. Bunchgrass and Ponderosa Pine are low winter country.

layers.label: Mule deer by month (general pattern)
layers.source: data/migration.json (cited studies) with BEC zones and elevation (terrarium tiles)
layers.about: Where mule deer tend to be by month: habitat zones and elevation bands from studies. General pattern, not mapped corridors. Use the month slider.

layers.about: Where white tailed deer tend to be by month: habitat zones and elevation bands from studies. General pattern, not mapped corridors. Use the month slider.

layers.label: Elk by month (general pattern)
layers.source: data/migration.json (cited studies) with BEC zones and elevation (terrarium tiles)

layers.label: Bighorn sheep by month (general pattern)
layers.source: data/migration.json (cited studies) with BEC zones and elevation (terrarium tiles)

layers.label: Duck staging and winter waters
layers.source: FWA lakes, wetlands and rivers with data/migration.json flyway timing
layers.about: Valley lakes and wetlands of 20 ha or more where ducks stop in fall and spring, and low open water in winter. General pattern.

layers.label: California quail habitat (no migration)
layers.source: BEC zones and elevation with data/migration.json
layers.about: Quail do not migrate. Low Bunchgrass and Ponderosa Pine country near farms and brushy creeks, all year. General pattern.

layers.label: Campgrounds and camp spots
legend: Rec site (Recreation Sites and Trails BC)
layers.source: Recreation Sites and Trails BC (FTEN_REC_SITE_POINTS_SVW), BC Parks API, OpenStreetMap (unofficial listings) and Hunt Mentor Crown land camp candidates
layers.about: Every campground and camp spot we can find in BC, by type. Tap one for the details and the source of each line.
layers.attribution: Rec sites and BC Parks: Open Government Licence BC. Other campgrounds: OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
layers.licence: Open Government Licence BC; Open Database License (ODbL), OpenStreetMap contributors

layers.label: Candidate spots
layers.source: Hunt Mentor spot pipeline (scripts/spots-pipeline.py) from BC Data Catalogue layers
layers.about: Candidate spots scored from open data (my pick): drive, ATV (all terrain vehicle), walk, backcountry and camp. Popular (more hunters) and Less popular (quieter) are estimates. Candidate, scout it first.

layers.label: Walk and ride routes
layers.source: Hunt Mentor spot pipeline (road atlas, forest roads, rec trails)
layers.about: Suggested approach lines (estimate).
